ruth.before: In the days when the judges judged, there was a famine in the land. A man went from Bethlehem in Judah to live as a resident alien in the fields of Moab, he and his wife and his two sons.
ruth.after: In the days when the judges judged, there was a famine in the land. A man from Bethlehem in Judah went to live as a foreigner in the fields of Moab, with his wife and his two sons.

ruth.before: The man’s name was Elimelech, his wife’s name was Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They came to the fields of Moab and were there.
ruth.after: The man’s name was Elimelech, his wife’s name was Naomi, and his two sons were named Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They came to the fields of Moab and stayed there.

ruth.before: Both Mahlon and Chilion also died, and the woman was left bereft of her two children and her husband.
ruth.after: Both Mahlon and Chilion also died, and the woman was left without her two children or her husband.

ruth.before: She arose with her daughters-in-law and returned from the fields of Moab, for she had heard in the field of Moab that YHWH had visited His people to give them bread.
ruth.after: She set out with her daughters-in-law to return from the fields of Moab, for in the country of Moab she had heard that YHWH had visited His people to give them bread.

ruth.before: She went out from the place where she had been, with her two daughters-in-law, and they took the road to return to the land of Judah.
ruth.after: She left the place where she had been, her two daughters-in-law with her, and they took the road back to the land of Judah.

ruth.before: Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go; return, each to her mother’s house. May YHWH show you steadfast kindness, as you have shown it to the dead and to me.
ruth.after: Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go back, each of you to your own mother’s house. May YHWH show you steadfast kindness, as you have shown it to the dead and to me.

ruth.before: Return, my daughters; go, for I am too old to have a husband. Even if I said, ‘I have hope,’ even if I had a husband tonight and even bore sons,
ruth.after: Go back, my daughters. Go, for I am too old to have a husband. Even if I said, ‘I have hope,’ even if I had a husband tonight and bore sons,

ruth.before: would you wait for them until they grew up? Would you shut yourselves away for them, without having a husband? No, my daughters. It is far more bitter for me than for you, for YHWH’s hand has gone out against me.”
ruth.after: would you wait for them until they grew up? Would you hold yourselves back from marrying for their sake? No, my daughters. It is far more bitter for me than for you, for the hand of YHWH has gone out against me.”

ruth.before: She said, “Look, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and to her gods. Return after your sister-in-law.”
ruth.after: She said, “Look, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and to her gods. Follow your sister-in-law back.”

ruth.before: Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May YHWH do this to me, and add more, for death will separate me and you.”
ruth.after: Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May YHWH do so to me, and more besides. Death alone will separate me from you.”

ruth.before: When she saw that she was determined to go with her, she stopped speaking to her.
ruth.after: When Naomi saw how determined Ruth was to go with her, she said no more to her.

ruth.before: So Naomi returned, with Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, who came back from the fields of Moab. They reached Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.
ruth.after: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, came back with her from the fields of Moab. They reached Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.

ruth.before: Naomi had a kinsman of her husband, a man of great standing from Elimelech’s clan, whose name was Boaz.
ruth.after: Now Naomi had a kinsman on her husband’s side, a man of great standing from Elimelech’s clan. His name was Boaz.

ruth.before: Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, “Please let me go to the field and glean among the ears of grain after someone in whose eyes I find favor.” She said to her, “Go, my daughter.”
ruth.after: Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, “Please let me go to the field and glean ears of grain behind someone in whose eyes I find favor.” She said to her, “Go, my daughter.”

ruth.before: She went, came to the field, and gleaned behind the reapers. As it happened, she happened upon the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was from Elimelech’s clan.
ruth.after: She went out to the field and gleaned behind the reapers. As chance would have it, she came upon the part of the field that belonged to Boaz, who was from Elimelech’s clan.

ruth.before: Boaz said to his young man who was stationed over the reapers, “Whose young woman is this?”
ruth.after: Boaz asked his young man in charge of the reapers, “Whose young woman is this?”

ruth.before: The young man stationed over the reapers answered and said, “She is a Moabite young woman who returned with Naomi from the field of Moab.
ruth.after: The young man in charge of the reapers answered, “She is the young Moabite woman who returned with Naomi from the fields of Moab.

ruth.before: She said, ‘Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the reapers.’ She came and has remained from the morning until now; her sitting in the shelter has been little.”
ruth.after: She said, ‘Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the reapers.’ She came and has stayed since morning, and has spent little time sitting in the house.”

ruth.before: Boaz said to Ruth, “Do you not hear, my daughter? Do not go to glean in another field, and do not pass on from here. Stay close here with my young women.
ruth.after: Boaz said to Ruth, “Have you not heard, my daughter? Do not go to glean in another field or leave this one. Stay close beside my young women here.

ruth.before: May YHWH repay your deed, and may your reward be complete from YHWH, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge.”
ruth.after: May YHWH repay you for what you have done, and may your reward come in full from YHWH, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge.”

ruth.before: She said, “May I find favor in your eyes, my lord, for you have comforted me and spoken to the heart of your slave woman, though I am not like one of your slave girls.”
ruth.after: She said, “May I find favor in your eyes, my lord. You have comforted me and spoken to the heart of your slave woman, though I am not one of your slave women.”

ruth.before: She arose to glean, and Boaz commanded his young men, saying, “Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not shame her.
ruth.after: She rose to glean, and Boaz commanded his young men, “Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not put her to shame.

ruth.before: You must also pull some out for her from the bundles and leave it; let her glean, and do not rebuke her.”
ruth.after: Be sure to pull some stalks from the bundles for her. Leave them for her to glean, and do not rebuke her.”

ruth.before: She lifted it and came into the city. Her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. She brought out and gave her what she had left after being satisfied.
ruth.after: She carried it into the city, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. Ruth brought out what was left after she had eaten her fill and gave it to her.

ruth.before: Ruth the Moabite said, “He also said to me, ‘Stay close with my young men until they have finished all my harvest.’”
ruth.after: Ruth the Moabite said, “He also told me, ‘Stay close to my young men until they have finished all my harvest.’”

ruth.before: Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, “It is good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, so that they do not accost you in another field.”
ruth.after: Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, “It is good, my daughter, for you to go out with his young women, so that no one harms you in another field.”

ruth.before: She stayed close to Boaz’s young women to glean until the barley harvest and the wheat harvest ended. She lived with her mother-in-law.
ruth.after: So she stayed close to Boaz’s young women to glean until the barley and wheat harvests were over. She lived with her mother-in-law.

ruth.before: Now, is not Boaz our kinsman, with whose young women you were? Look, he is winnowing the barley on the threshing floor tonight.
ruth.after: Now, is Boaz not our kinsman, the one whose young women you were with? Look, tonight he is winnowing barley at the threshing floor.

ruth.before: Wash, anoint yourself, put your garments on, and go down to the threshing floor. Do not make yourself known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking.
ruth.after: Wash, anoint yourself, put on your garments, and go down to the threshing floor. Do not make yourself known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking.

ruth.before: When he lies down, notice the place where he lies. Go in, uncover the place at his feet, and lie down. He will tell you what you should do.”
ruth.after: When he lies down, take note of where he lies. Go in, uncover the place at his feet, and lie down. He will tell you what to do.”

ruth.before: She said to her, “Everything you say to me I will do.”
ruth.after: She answered, “I will do everything you tell me.”

ruth.before: At midnight the man was startled and turned over, and look, a woman was lying at his feet.
ruth.after: At midnight the man was startled and turned over, and there at his feet lay a woman.

ruth.before: He said, “Blessed be you by YHWH, my daughter. You have made this last kindness greater than the first, by not going after young men, whether poor or rich.
ruth.after: He said, “May you be blessed by YHWH, my daughter. The kindness you have shown now is greater than the first, for you did not go after young men, whether poor or rich.

ruth.before: Now, my daughter, do not fear. Everything you say I will do for you, for all my people at the gate know that you are a woman of worth.
ruth.after: Do not be afraid, my daughter. I will do for you all that you say, for all my people at the gate know that you are a woman of worth.

ruth.before: Now, it is indeed true that I am a redeeming kinsman, but there is also a redeeming kinsman nearer than I.
ruth.after: I am indeed a redeeming kinsman, but there is also a redeeming kinsman nearer than I am.

ruth.before: Stay the night. In the morning, if he will redeem you, good; let him redeem you. But if he does not wish to redeem you, I will redeem you, as YHWH lives. Lie down until morning.”
ruth.after: Stay the night. In the morning, if he will redeem you, well and good. Let him redeem you. But if he does not wish to redeem you, I will redeem you, as YHWH lives. Lie down until morning.”

ruth.before: She lay at his feet until morning and arose before a man could recognize his neighbor. He said, “Let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor.”
ruth.after: She lay at his feet until morning and rose before one person could recognize another. He said, “Let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor.”

ruth.before: He said, “Bring the wrap you are wearing and hold it.” She held it, and he measured six measures of barley and laid it on her. He entered the city.
ruth.after: He said, “Bring the wrap you are wearing and hold it out.” She held it, and he measured out six measures of barley and laid it on her. Then he went into the city.

ruth.before: She said, “Sit, my daughter, until you know how the matter will turn out, for the man will not rest unless he finishes the matter today.”
ruth.after: She said, “Wait, my daughter, until you know how the matter will turn out. The man will not rest until he has settled it today.”

ruth.before: Boaz went up to the gate and sat there. Look, the redeeming kinsman of whom Boaz had spoken was passing by. He said, “Turn aside and sit here, so-and-so.” He turned aside and sat down.
ruth.after: Boaz went up to the gate and sat there. Just then, the redeeming kinsman Boaz had spoken of passed by. Boaz said, “Come aside and sit here, so-and-so.” He came aside and sat down.

ruth.before: He took ten men from the city’s elders and said, “Sit here.” They sat down.
ruth.after: Boaz took ten men from among the elders of the city and said, “Sit here.” They sat down.

ruth.before: He said to the redeeming kinsman, “Naomi, who returned from the field of Moab, has sold the portion of the field that belonged to our brother Elimelech.
ruth.after: He said to the redeeming kinsman, “Naomi, who returned from the country of Moab, has put up for sale the part of the field that belonged to our brother Elimelech.

ruth.before: I thought I should uncover your ear, saying, ‘Acquire it before those seated here and before my people’s elders.’ If you will redeem it, redeem it; but if he will not redeem it, tell me, so that I may know, for there is no one besides you to redeem it, and I come after you.” He said, “I will redeem it.”
ruth.after: I thought I should tell you and say, ‘Acquire it before those sitting here and before the elders of my people.’ If you will redeem it, redeem it. But if he will not redeem it, tell me so that I may know, for there is no one besides you to redeem it, and I come after you.” He said, “I will redeem it.”

ruth.before: Boaz said, “On the day you acquire the field from Naomi’s hand, you also acquire from Ruth the Moabite, the dead man’s wife, to raise up the dead man’s name upon his inheritance.”
ruth.after: Boaz said, “On the day you acquire the field from Naomi’s hand, you acquire it also from Ruth the Moabite, the dead man’s wife, to keep the dead man’s name alive on his inheritance.”

ruth.before: The redeeming kinsman said, “I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I ruin my inheritance. Redeem for yourself my right of redemption, for I cannot redeem it.”
ruth.after: The redeeming kinsman said, “I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I ruin my own inheritance. Exercise my right of redemption for yourself, for I cannot redeem it.”

ruth.before: This was the practice formerly in Israel concerning redemption and exchange, to confirm every matter: a man removed his sandal and gave it to his neighbor. This was the attestation in Israel.
ruth.after: Formerly in Israel, to confirm a matter of redemption or exchange, a man would take off his sandal and give it to his neighbor. This was the way of attesting it in Israel.

ruth.before: The redeeming kinsman said to Boaz, “Acquire it for yourself.” He removed his sandal.
ruth.after: The redeeming kinsman said to Boaz, “Acquire it for yourself.” Then he took off his sandal.

ruth.before: I have also acquired Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon’s wife, as my wife, to raise up the dead man’s name upon his inheritance, so that the dead man’s name will not be cut off from among his brothers and from the gate of his place. You are witnesses today.”
ruth.after: I have also acquired Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon’s wife, as my wife, to keep the dead man’s name alive on his inheritance, so that the dead man’s name will not be cut off from among his brothers or from the gate of his town. You are witnesses today.”

ruth.before: All the people at the gate and the elders said, “We are witnesses. May YHWH make the woman entering your house like Rachel and Leah, who together built Israel’s house. May you act worthily in Ephrathah and make a name in Bethlehem.
ruth.after: All the people at the gate and the elders said, “We are witnesses. May YHWH make the woman coming into your house like Rachel and Leah, who both built the house of Israel. May you act worthily in Ephrathah and make a name in Bethlehem.

ruth.before: Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. He went in to her, and YHWH gave her conception, and she bore a son.
ruth.after: Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. He went in to her, and YHWH granted that she conceive, and she bore a son.

ruth.before: The women said to Naomi, “Blessed be YHWH, who has not left you without a redeeming kinsman today. May his name be called in Israel.
ruth.after: The women said to Naomi, “Blessed be YHWH, who has not left you without a redeeming kinsman today. May his name be proclaimed in Israel.

ruth.before: He shall be to you a restorer of life and a sustainer of your old age, for your daughter-in-law, who loves you and is better to you than seven sons, has borne him.”
ruth.after: He will restore your life and sustain you in your old age, for your daughter-in-law, who loves you and is better to you than seven sons, has borne him.”

ruth.before: Naomi took the child, placed him in her bosom, and became his nurse.
ruth.after: Naomi took the child and laid him in her lap, and from then on she cared for him.

ruth.before: The neighboring women gave him a name, saying, “A son has been born to Naomi.” They called his name Obed. He was the father of Jesse, the father of David.
ruth.after: The neighboring women gave him a name, saying, “A son has been born to Naomi.” They named him Obed. He was the father of Jesse, the father of David.

ruth.before: These are the generations of Perez: Perez begat Hezron,
ruth.after: These are the generations of Perez. Perez fathered Hezron,

ruth.before: Hezron begat Ram, and Ram begat Amminadab,
ruth.after: Hezron fathered Ram, and Ram fathered Amminadab,

ruth.before: Amminadab begat Nahshon, and Nahshon begat Salmah,
ruth.after: Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmah,

ruth.before: Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed,
ruth.after: Salmon fathered Boaz, and Boaz fathered Obed,

ruth.before: Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David.
ruth.after: Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.

jonah.before: But Jonah rose to flee to Tarshish from the presence of YHWH. He went down to Joppa, found a ship going to Tarshish, paid its fare and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish from the presence of YHWH.
jonah.after: But Jonah rose to flee to Tarshish from the presence of YHWH. He went down to Joppa and found a ship bound for Tarshish. He paid its fare and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish from the presence of YHWH.

jonah.before: YHWH hurled a great wind upon the sea, and there was a great storm on the sea; the ship threatened to break apart.
jonah.after: But YHWH hurled a great wind upon the sea, and a great storm arose on the sea. The ship threatened to break apart.

jonah.before: The sailors were afraid, and each cried out to his god. They hurled the equipment that was in the ship into the sea, to lighten it for themselves. But Jonah had gone down into the recesses of the ship, lain down and fallen deeply asleep.
jonah.after: The sailors were afraid, and each cried out to his god. They hurled the gear from the ship into the sea to lighten their load. But Jonah had gone down into the depths of the ship, where he lay down and fell fast asleep.

jonah.before: The captain approached him and said, “What are you doing, sound asleep? Rise, call to your god! Perhaps the god will give thought to us, and we will not perish.”
jonah.after: The captain came to him and said, “What are you doing asleep? Rise and call to your god! Perhaps the god will take notice of us, and we will not perish.”

jonah.before: They said to him, “Tell us, please, on whose account is this disaster upon us? What is your occupation, and where do you come from? What is your country, and from what people are you?”
jonah.after: They said to him, “Please tell us, on whose account has this disaster come upon us? What is your work? Where do you come from? What is your country, and what people do you belong to?”

jonah.before: The men were greatly afraid and said to him, “What is this you have done?” For the men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of YHWH, because he had told them.
jonah.after: The men were filled with great fear and said to him, “What have you done?” For the men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of YHWH, because he had told them.

jonah.before: They said to him, “What shall we do to you, so that the sea may become quiet for us?” For the sea was growing more and more stormy.
jonah.after: They said to him, “What shall we do to you so that the sea will calm down for us?” For the sea was growing more and more stormy.

jonah.before: He said to them, “Lift me up and hurl me into the sea; then the sea will become quiet for you. For I know that this great storm is upon you because of me.”
jonah.after: He said to them, “Lift me up and hurl me into the sea. Then the sea will calm down for you, for I know that this great storm has come upon you because of me.”

jonah.before: But the men rowed hard to bring the ship back to dry land, and they could not, for the sea was growing more and more stormy against them.
jonah.after: But the men rowed hard to get back to dry land. They could not, for the sea was growing more and more stormy against them.

jonah.before: They called to YHWH and said, “Please, YHWH, do not let us perish for this man's life, and do not lay innocent blood upon us; for You, YHWH, have done as You pleased.”
jonah.after: They called to YHWH and said, “Please, YHWH, do not let us perish for the life of this man, and do not lay innocent blood upon us. For You, YHWH, have done as You pleased.”

jonah.before: They lifted Jonah up and hurled him into the sea, and the sea stopped its raging.
jonah.after: They lifted Jonah up and hurled him into the sea, and the sea ceased its raging.

jonah.before: The men feared YHWH with great fear, offered a sacrifice to YHWH and made vows.
jonah.after: The men feared YHWH greatly. They offered a sacrifice to YHWH and made vows.

jonah.before: YHWH appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the fish's belly three days and three nights.
jonah.after: YHWH appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish for three days and three nights.

jonah.before: Jonah prayed to YHWH his God from the fish's belly.
jonah.after: Jonah prayed to YHWH his God from the belly of the fish.

jonah.before: He said: “From my distress I called to YHWH, and He answered me. From the belly of Sheol I cried for help; You heard my voice.
jonah.after: He said, “Out of my distress I called to YHWH, and He answered me. From the belly of Sheol I cried for help, and You heard my voice.

jonah.before: I said, ‘I have been driven away from before Your eyes; yet I will again look toward Your holy temple.’
jonah.after: Then I said, ‘I have been driven from Your sight. Yet I will look again toward Your holy temple.’

jonah.before: Waters enclosed me up to my life; the deep surrounded me; seaweed was wrapped around my head.
jonah.after: The waters closed in up to my throat. The deep surrounded me, and seaweed wrapped around my head.

jonah.before: I descended to the bases of the mountains. The earth—its bars were around me forever. Yet You brought my life up from the pit, YHWH my God.
jonah.after: I went down to the roots of the mountains. The earth shut its bars behind me forever. Yet You brought my life up from the pit, YHWH my God.

jonah.before: When my life was fainting within me, I remembered YHWH; my prayer came to You, to Your holy temple.
jonah.after: When my life was ebbing away, I remembered YHWH, and my prayer came to You, to Your holy temple.

jonah.before: Those who attend to empty vanities forsake their steadfast love.
jonah.after: Those who cling to empty idols forsake the steadfast love that is theirs.

jonah.before: But I, with a voice of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to You. What I vowed I will fulfill. Salvation belongs to YHWH!”
jonah.after: But I will sacrifice to You with a voice of thanksgiving. What I have vowed I will fulfill. Salvation belongs to YHWH!”

jonah.before: “Rise, go to Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim to it the proclamation that I speak to you.”
jonah.after: “Rise, go to Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim to it the message I am giving you.”

jonah.before: Jonah rose and went to Nineveh according to the word of YHWH. Now Nineveh was a city great before God, a journey of three days.
jonah.after: Jonah rose and went to Nineveh as YHWH had told him. Now Nineveh was a city great before God, a journey of three days.

jonah.before: Jonah began to enter the city, a journey of one day, and he proclaimed: “Forty more days, and Nineveh will be overturned!”
jonah.after: Jonah began to go into the city, a day’s journey. He cried out, “Forty more days, and Nineveh will be overturned!”

jonah.before: The people of Nineveh believed God, proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from their greatest to their least.
jonah.after: The people of Nineveh believed God. They proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them to the least.

jonah.before: The word reached the king of Nineveh. He rose from his throne, removed his robe, covered himself in sackcloth and sat in ashes.
jonah.after: The word reached the king of Nineveh. He rose from his throne, took off his robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.

jonah.before: He had this proclaimed and declared in Nineveh: “By decree of the king and his nobles: Let neither people nor livestock, neither herd nor flock, taste anything. Let them not graze or drink water.
jonah.after: He had this proclaimed and declared in Nineveh: “By decree of the king and his nobles, let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste anything. Let them neither graze nor drink water.

jonah.before: Let people and livestock cover themselves with sackcloth, and let them call mightily to God. Let each turn from his evil way and from the violence in their hands.
jonah.after: Let people and beasts be covered with sackcloth, and let them call to God with all their might. Let each turn from his evil way and from the violence in their hands.

jonah.before: God saw their deeds, that they had turned from their evil way. God relented concerning the disaster He had said He would bring upon them, and He did not do it.
jonah.after: God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil way. God relented concerning the disaster He had said He would bring upon them, and He did not bring it.

jonah.before: This was a great evil in Jonah's eyes, and he became angry.
jonah.after: This seemed a great wrong to Jonah, and he became angry.

jonah.before: He prayed to YHWH and said, “Please, YHWH, was this not what I said while I was still in my own land? That is why I hastened to flee to Tarshish: I knew that You are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger, abundant in steadfast love, and relenting concerning disaster.
jonah.after: He prayed to YHWH and said, “Please, YHWH, is this not what I said while I was still in my own land? That is why I made haste to flee to Tarshish. I knew that You are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger and abundant in steadfast love, and that You relent from bringing disaster.

jonah.before: And now, YHWH, please take my life from me, for my death is better than my life.”
jonah.after: Now, YHWH, please take my life from me, for it is better for me to die than to live.”

jonah.before: Jonah went out of the city and sat east of the city. He made himself a shelter there and sat under it in the shade, until he could see what would happen in the city.
jonah.after: Jonah went out of the city and sat down to its east. There he made himself a shelter and sat under it in the shade until he could see what would happen in the city.

jonah.before: YHWH God appointed a qiqayon plant and made it rise over Jonah, to provide shade over his head and rescue him from his misery. Jonah rejoiced over the qiqayon with great joy.
jonah.after: YHWH God appointed a qiqayon plant and made it grow up over Jonah to shade his head and deliver him from his misery. Jonah was exceedingly glad about the plant.

jonah.before: God appointed a worm at the rise of dawn the next day; it struck the qiqayon, and it withered.
jonah.after: At dawn the next day God appointed a worm, and it struck the plant, and the plant withered.

jonah.before: When the sun rose, God appointed a scorching east wind. The sun struck Jonah's head, and he grew faint. He asked that his life might end and said, “My death is better than my life.”
jonah.after: When the sun rose, God appointed a scorching east wind. The sun beat upon Jonah’s head, and he grew faint. He asked to die and said, “It is better for me to die than to live.”

jonah.before: God said to Jonah, “Is it right for you to be angry about the qiqayon?” He said, “It is right for me to be angry, even to death.”
jonah.after: God said to Jonah, “Is it right for you to be angry about the plant?” He said, “It is right for me to be angry, even to the point of death.”

jonah.before: YHWH said, “You had pity on the qiqayon, for which you did not labor and which you did not grow, which came to be in a night and perished in a night.
jonah.after: YHWH said, “You had pity on the plant, though you did not labor over it or make it grow. It sprang up in a night and perished in a night.

jonah.before: And should I not have pity on Nineveh, the great city, in which there are more than one hundred and twenty thousand people who do not know their right hand from their left, and much livestock?”
jonah.after: And should I not have pity on Nineveh, the great city, where there are more than one hundred and twenty thousand people who do not know their right hand from their left, and many animals?”

habakkuk.before: How long, YHWH, have I cried for help and You do not hear? I cry to You, “Violence!” and You do not save.
habakkuk.after: How long, YHWH, must I cry for help while You do not hear? I cry to You, “Violence!” and You do not save.

habakkuk.before: Why do You make me see wrongdoing, and why do You look upon misery? Destruction and violence are before me; strife arises and contention lifts itself up.
habakkuk.after: Why do You make me see wrongdoing? Why do You look on misery? Destruction and violence are before me. Strife breaks out and contention rises.

habakkuk.before: Therefore instruction grows numb, and justice never goes forth; the wicked surrounds the righteous, so justice goes forth twisted.
habakkuk.after: So the law grows numb, and justice never goes forth. The wicked surround the righteous, and so justice comes out twisted.

habakkuk.before: Look among the nations and observe; be utterly astonished! For a work is being done in your days that you would not believe if it were told.
habakkuk.after: Look among the nations and see. Be utterly astonished! For a work is being done in your days that you would not believe if you were told.

habakkuk.before: For look, I am raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter and impetuous nation, who traverse the breadth of the earth to possess dwellings not their own.
habakkuk.after: For look, I am raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter and impetuous nation. They cross the breadth of the earth to take possession of homes that are not their own.

habakkuk.before: Dreadful and fearsome are they; their judgment and dignity proceed from themselves.
habakkuk.after: They are dreadful and fearsome. Their justice and dignity come from themselves.

habakkuk.before: Their horses are swifter than leopards and fiercer than wolves at evening. Their horsemen spread out; their horsemen come from afar, flying like an eagle hastening to eat.
habakkuk.after: Their horses are swifter than leopards and fiercer than wolves at dusk. Their horsemen spread out. Their horsemen come from afar, flying like an eagle rushing to devour.

habakkuk.before: All of them come for violence, their faces pressing eastward; they gather captives like sand.
habakkuk.after: They all come for violence, their faces pressing forward. They gather captives like sand.

habakkuk.before: They mock kings and make rulers a laughingstock. They laugh at every fortress, heap up earth and capture it.
habakkuk.after: They mock kings, and rulers are a laughingstock to them. They laugh at every fortress, heap up earth, and capture it.

habakkuk.before: Then they sweep on like wind and pass through, and incur guilt—those whose own strength is their god.
habakkuk.after: Then they sweep by like the wind and pass on. They incur guilt, for their own strength is their god.

habakkuk.before: Are You not from of old, YHWH my God, my Holy One? We shall not die. YHWH, You appointed him for judgment; Rock, You established him for correction.
habakkuk.after: Are You not from of old, YHWH my God, my Holy One? We shall not die. YHWH, You appointed them for judgment. O Rock, You established them for correction.

habakkuk.before: Your eyes are too pure to see evil, and You cannot look upon misery. Why do You look upon the treacherous and remain silent when the wicked swallows someone more righteous than himself?
habakkuk.after: Your eyes are too pure to see evil, and You cannot look upon misery. Why then do You look upon the treacherous? Why do You keep silent when the wicked swallow up those more righteous than themselves?

habakkuk.before: You make humanity like the fish of the sea, like creeping things with no ruler over them.
habakkuk.after: You make people like the fish of the sea, like creatures that creep with no ruler over them.

habakkuk.before: They bring all of them up with a hook, drag them in their net and gather them in their dragnet; therefore they rejoice and exult.
habakkuk.after: They pull them all up with a hook, drag them in with their net, and gather them in their dragnet. So they rejoice and exult.

habakkuk.before: Therefore they sacrifice to their net and burn incense to their dragnet, for through them their portion is rich and their food plentiful.
habakkuk.after: So they sacrifice to their net and burn incense to their dragnet, for by these their portion is rich and their food plentiful.

habakkuk.before: Will they therefore keep emptying their net, continually slaughtering nations without pity?
habakkuk.after: Will they then keep emptying their net, killing nations continually and without pity?

habakkuk.before: I will stand at my watch and station myself on the rampart; I will watch to see what He will speak within me and what I shall answer concerning my complaint.
habakkuk.after: I will stand at my post and station myself on the rampart. I will watch to see what He will say to me, and what I will answer concerning my complaint.

habakkuk.before: YHWH answered me: “Write the vision and make it plain on tablets, so that the one reading it may run.
habakkuk.after: YHWH answered me and said, “Write the vision and make it plain on the tablets, so that whoever reads it may run.

habakkuk.before: For the vision is still for an appointed time; it presses toward the end and will not lie. If it delays, wait for it, for it will surely come; it will not be late.
habakkuk.after: For the vision is still for the appointed time. It presses toward the end and will not lie. If it delays, wait for it. It will surely come and will not be late.

habakkuk.before: Look, his soul is swollen, not upright within him; but the righteous one will live by his faithfulness.
habakkuk.after: Look, he is puffed up, and his soul is not upright within him. But the righteous will live by his faithfulness.

habakkuk.before: Moreover, wine betrays the arrogant man, and he does not stay at home. He enlarges his appetite like Sheol and is like death, never satisfied; he gathers all nations and collects all peoples to himself.
habakkuk.after: Indeed, wine betrays the arrogant man, and he does not stay at home. He makes his appetite as wide as Sheol. Like death, he is never satisfied. He gathers all nations to himself and collects all peoples for himself.

habakkuk.before: Will not all these take up a taunt against him, a mocking riddle about him, and say, “Woe to the one increasing what is not his—how long?—and loading himself with pledges!”
habakkuk.after: Will not all these take up a taunt against him, a mocking riddle about him? They will say, ‘Woe to him who piles up what is not his! How long will he load himself down with pledges?’

habakkuk.before: Will not your creditors suddenly rise and your tormentors awake? You will become plunder for them.
habakkuk.after: Will not your creditors rise suddenly? Will not those who make you tremble wake up? Then you will be their plunder.

habakkuk.before: Because you plundered many nations, all the remaining peoples will plunder you, because of human bloodshed and violence against land, city and all its inhabitants.
habakkuk.after: Because you plundered many nations, all the peoples who remain will plunder you, because of human bloodshed and the violence done to the land, the city, and all who live in it.

habakkuk.before: Woe to the one gaining evil gain for his house, setting his nest on high to escape the hand of evil!
habakkuk.after: Woe to him who makes wicked gains for his house, who sets his nest on high to escape the grasp of evil!

habakkuk.before: You planned shame for your house by cutting off many peoples and sinning against your own life.
habakkuk.after: You have planned shame for your house by cutting off many peoples. You sin against your own life.

habakkuk.before: For a stone will cry from the wall, and a beam from the timber will answer it.
habakkuk.after: For a stone will cry out from the wall, and a beam from the timber will answer it.

habakkuk.before: Woe to the one building a city with bloodshed and establishing a town with injustice!
habakkuk.after: Woe to him who builds a city with bloodshed and establishes a town with injustice!

habakkuk.before: Look, is this not from YHWH of hosts: peoples labor only for fire, and nations weary themselves for nothing?
habakkuk.after: Look, is it not from YHWH of hosts that peoples labor for the fire, and nations wear themselves out for nothing?

habakkuk.before: Woe to the one making his neighbor drink, adding your fury and making him drunk, to look upon their nakedness!
habakkuk.after: Woe to him who gives his neighbor drink! You add your fury and make him drunk, so that you may look on their nakedness.

habakkuk.before: You are filled with shame instead of glory. Drink, you too, and expose your uncircumcision! The cup in YHWH's right hand will come round to you, and disgraceful vomit upon your glory.
habakkuk.after: You have had your fill of shame instead of glory. Drink, you too, and show your uncircumcision! The cup in YHWH’s right hand will come round to you, and foul vomit will cover your glory.

habakkuk.before: For violence against Lebanon will cover you, and the destruction of animals will terrify them, because of human bloodshed and violence against land, city and all its inhabitants.
habakkuk.after: For the violence done to Lebanon will cover you, and the destruction of the animals will terrify them, because of human bloodshed and the violence done to the land, the city, and all who live in it.

habakkuk.before: What use is a carved image, that its maker carved it, a cast image and teacher of lies, that its maker trusts his own creation, making speechless idols?
habakkuk.after: What good is a carved image, that its maker carves it? What good is a cast image that teaches lies, that its maker trusts what he has made? He makes idols that cannot speak.

habakkuk.before: Woe to the one saying to wood, ‘Awake!’ and to silent stone, ‘Rise!’ Can it teach? Look, it is overlaid with gold and silver, but there is no breath at all within it.
habakkuk.after: Woe to him who says to wood, ‘Awake!’ and to silent stone, ‘Rise!’ Can it teach? Look, it is overlaid with gold and silver, but there is no breath within it.

habakkuk.before: But YHWH is in His holy temple; be silent before Him, all the earth.”
habakkuk.after: But YHWH is in His holy temple. Let all the earth be silent before Him.”

habakkuk.before: YHWH, I have heard the report of You; I fear. YHWH, revive Your work in the midst of the years; in the midst of the years make it known. In wrath remember mercy.
habakkuk.after: YHWH, I have heard the report of You, and I fear. YHWH, revive Your work in the midst of the years. In the midst of the years make it known. In wrath remember mercy.

habakkuk.before: His radiance is like light; rays extend from His hand, and there His strength is hidden.
habakkuk.after: His radiance is like light. Rays come from His hand, and there His strength lies hidden.

habakkuk.before: Before Him goes pestilence, and plague follows at His feet.
habakkuk.after: Pestilence goes before Him, and plague goes out at His feet.

habakkuk.before: He stands and measures the earth; He looks and shakes nations loose. Ancient mountains shatter, everlasting hills sink down; His ways are everlasting.
habakkuk.after: He stands and measures the earth. He looks and makes nations tremble. The ancient mountains shatter, and the everlasting hills sink down. His ways are everlasting.

habakkuk.before: I saw the tents of Cushan under affliction; the curtains of the land of Midian trembled.
habakkuk.after: I saw the tents of Cushan in distress. The tent curtains of the land of Midian trembled.

habakkuk.before: Was YHWH angry with the rivers? Was Your anger against rivers, or Your fury against the sea, when You rode Your horses, Your chariots of salvation?
habakkuk.after: Was YHWH angry with the rivers? Was Your anger against the rivers, or Your fury against the sea, when You rode upon Your horses, upon Your chariots of salvation?

habakkuk.before: Your bow is fully bared; sworn oaths of rods—the word! Selah. You split the earth with rivers.
habakkuk.after: Your bow is laid bare. Oaths are sworn for the shafts at Your word. Selah. You split the earth with rivers.

habakkuk.before: Mountains saw You and writhed; a torrent of water passed. The deep gave its voice and lifted its hands on high.
habakkuk.after: The mountains saw You and writhed. A torrent of water swept past. The deep lifted its voice and raised its hands on high.

habakkuk.before: Sun and moon stand in their dwelling; at the light of Your arrows they move, at the brightness of Your flashing spear.
habakkuk.after: Sun and moon stand in their dwelling. At the light of Your arrows they move, at the gleam of Your flashing spear.

habakkuk.before: You went out for Your people's salvation, for salvation with Your anointed. You crushed the head of the wicked house, exposing its foundation up to the neck. Selah.
habakkuk.after: You went out for the salvation of Your people, for the salvation of Your anointed. You crushed the head of the house of the wicked, laying it bare from its foundation up to the neck. Selah.

habakkuk.before: You pierced the head of his warriors with his own rods; they stormed out to scatter me, exulting as though to devour the poor in secret.
habakkuk.after: You pierced the head of his warriors with his own shafts. They stormed out to scatter me, rejoicing as if to devour the poor in secret.

habakkuk.before: You trod the sea with Your horses, the surging of mighty waters.
habakkuk.after: You trod the sea with Your horses, the surging mass of mighty waters.

habakkuk.before: I heard, and my belly trembled; at the sound my lips quivered. Rot entered my bones, and I trembled where I stood, that I might rest on the day of distress when it comes upon the people who raid us.
habakkuk.after: I heard, and my belly trembled. At the sound my lips quivered. Rot entered my bones, and I trembled where I stood. I wait quietly for the day of distress to come upon the people who raid us.

habakkuk.before: Though the fig tree does not blossom, and there is no yield on vines; though the olive's labor fails and fields produce no food, the flock is cut off from the fold and no cattle remain in stalls,
habakkuk.after: Though the fig tree does not blossom and the vines yield nothing, though the olive crop fails and the fields produce no food, though the flock is cut off from the fold and there are no cattle in the stalls,

habakkuk.before: yet I will exult in YHWH; I will rejoice in the God of my salvation.
habakkuk.after: yet I will exult in YHWH. I will rejoice in the God of my salvation.

habakkuk.before: YHWH the Lord is my strength; He makes my feet like does' feet and leads me upon my heights. For the director, with my stringed music.
habakkuk.after: YHWH the Lord is my strength. He makes my feet like a doe’s and makes me tread upon my heights. For the director, with my stringed instruments.
